claims.claim: The style is unstable, veering from functional modern thriller prose to prose larded with fake medievalisms and from an Anglo-Saxon to a Latinate lexicon.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014
claims.quote: veers from purely functional modern thriller prose

claims.claim: The default setting of the style is lucid and functional.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014
claims.quote: The default setting of Martin’s style is lucid and functional

claims.claim: Martin consistently chooses Anglo-Saxon words over Latinate ones, giving the prose a cumulative woodiness, antiquity and pithiness.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014
claims.quote: a cumulative feeling of woodiness, antiquity, pithiness

claims.claim: 'Oft', 'elsewise', 'amongst', 'whilst', 'much and more' and dropped -ly adverbs become annoying pseudo-medieval mannerisms.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014

claims.claim: Distorted words ('Ser', girls who have 'flowered') start silly but by sheer repetition come to seem natural.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014
claims.quote: by sheer repetition, comes to seem the natural term

claims.claim: Compounds like sellsword, smallfolk, ironborn, greenseer and weirwood are a highly creative and enjoyable aspect of the style.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014
claims.quote: a highly creative and enjoyable aspect of his style

claims.claim: Confrontations are done through terse, charged dialogue that delivers real dramatic shock.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014

claims.claim: Repeated 'cool' and 'still' in the Water Gardens passage may be haste or deliberate torpor-evoking repetition.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014
claims.quote: signs of haste, or careful repetitions

claims.claim: Names in three registers (near-familiar, alien, exotic) work on a purely verbal level to pull the reader into a parallel universe.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014
claims.quote: the text works on a purely verbal level

claims.claim: The style is uneven but often wonderfully powerful and evocative.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'Some notes on George RR Martin's prose style', 31 Mar 2014
claims.quote: uneven but often wonderfully powerful and evocative

claims.claim: The archaic feel comes from the systematic exclusion of almost all Latin-, Greek- and French-derived words.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'George RR Martin's prose style – Affixes, compound and combination words', 8 Mar 2013
claims.quote: a systematic exclusion from his vocabulary of almost all words

claims.claim: Martin uses almost exclusively English prefixes (un-, be-, a-) and native suffixes (-craft, -dom, -ling, -ward).
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'George RR Martin's prose style – Affixes, compound and combination words', 8 Mar 2013
claims.quote: Martin uses almost exclusively English (i.e. Anglo-Saxon) prefixes

claims.claim: Anglo-Saxon compounding lets Martin coin scores of evocative neologisms (archmaester, bannermen, skinchanger, weirwood).
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'George RR Martin's prose style – Affixes, compound and combination words', 8 Mar 2013
claims.quote: scores of wonderful and evocative neologisms

claims.claim: The result is prose that feels archaic; the medieval sense comes from filtered vocabulary, not stock phrases.
claims.source: Simon (Books & Boots), 'George RR Martin's prose style – Affixes, compound and combination words', 8 Mar 2013
claims.quote: The result is to make his prose feel archaic

claims.claim: Martin leans on words he thinks sound archaic and exotic, which in reality sound ridiculous.
claims.source: Asher Gelzer-Govatos, 'The Literary Crimes of George R.R. Martin', The Erstwhile Philistine, 21 Mar 2012
claims.quote: words that I presume he thinks sound archaic and exotic
